title: Existence of the normalized common-stage tensor associator satisfying its prescribed finite-stage equations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme $W$ with $\ell$ invertible in every residue field. Use the intrinsic rational finite-coefficient stages and their fixed scalar stage system [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages], and its pair category $\mathcal C_W$ [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Its objects are pairs $(E,K)$ for finite $E\subset\Omega$, with arrows the common-stage classes $[L,u]$. Use the actual common-stage tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]: $(E,K)\otimes(F,H)$ has stage $EF$ and object $K_{EF}\otimes_{EF}H_{EF}$, with the prescribed scalar/tensor comparison $c_{A,B;L}:(A\otimes B)_L\xrightarrow{\sim}A_L\otimes_L B_L$ including the input stage associators. Finite coefficient composita are those of [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Let $M,N,P\in\mathcal C_W$ and put $S=(M\otimes N)\otimes P$, $T=M\otimes(N\otimes P)$. For every finite coefficient field $L$ containing the stages of both $S$ and $T$, define
$$\lambda_L=c_{M\otimes N,P;L};(c_{M,N;L}\otimes_L1):S_L\xrightarrow{\sim}(M_L\otimes_LN_L)\otimes_LP_L,$$
$$\rho_L=c_{M,N\otimes P;L};(1\otimes_Lc_{N,P;L}):T_L\xrightarrow{\sim}M_L\otimes_L(N_L\otimes_LP_L).$$
Thus $\lambda_L$ and $\rho_L$ are exactly pullbackTensorCommonLeft and pullbackTensorCommonRight. Write $\alpha^L$ for the rational localization of the coherent-reduction-normalized integral associator [def-pod-integral-tensor-constraints]. There exists an isomorphism $e:S\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ such that, for every such $L$,
$$e^{\mathrm{hom}}=[L,\lambda_L;\alpha^L_{M_L,N_L,P_L};\rho_L^{-1}].$$
The equality is in the actual pair category, equivalently the HEq with ofHom in pullbackTensorCommonAssociator_exists. The assertion is existence with all prescribed representative equations, and does not assert uniqueness.

proof.text: Choose $L_0$ to be the compositum of the stages of $S$ and $T$. Both stages contain the input fields, so all displayed input extensions and both nested comparisons exist. Put $u_L=\lambda_L;\alpha^L;\rho_L^{-1}$ whenever $L$ contains these stages. The prescribed rational associator is an isomorphism, so $u_L$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $v_L=\rho_L;(\alpha^L)^{-1};\lambda_L^{-1}$. These are maps $S_L\to T_L$ and $T_L\to S_L$, respectively. This uses the actual nested comparisons in the statement, not a choice of a tensor structure on the pair category.

proof.text:
For $L\subseteq H$ write $B=B_{H/L}$ and $\delta_A:B(A_L)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_H$ for the fixed stage associator of any pair $A$. Let $\beta^{\mathrm l}:B((M_L\otimes N_L)\otimes P_L)\to(M_H\otimes N_H)\otimes P_H$ be $b^{\mathrm l}$ followed by $((\delta_M\otimes\delta_N)\otimes\delta_P)$; define $\beta^{\mathrm r}$ using $b^{\mathrm r}$ followed by $(\delta_M\otimes(\delta_N\otimes\delta_P))$. Expand each binary $c_{A,B;L}$: it is the scalar tensor comparison after extending from the compositum, followed by the tensor of the two input stage associators. The FamilyTower equation combines the two successive scalar tensor comparisons into the direct one; the stage cocycle combines each successive input associator into its direct associator. Naturality of the binary comparison moves those input associators past it. Applied to the two binary vertices of each nested expression, these substitutions give
$$\delta_S;\lambda_H=B(\lambda_L);\beta^{\mathrm l},\qquad \delta_T;\rho_H=B(\rho_L);\beta^{\mathrm r}.$$
Only expansion of the defined $c$ and the two cited tower equations is involved; no compatibility of $\alpha$ has been used here.

proof.text:
The finite-field scalar square gives $B(\alpha^L);b^{\mathrm r}=b^{\mathrm l};\alpha^H_{BM_L,BN_L,BP_L}$. Naturality of the same associator with respect to $\delta_M,\delta_N,\delta_P$ therefore gives
$$B(\alpha^L);\beta^{\mathrm r}=\beta^{\mathrm l};\alpha^H_{M_H,N_H,P_H}.$$
The prescribed transport of an arrow $S_L\to T_L$ to $H$ is $\delta_S^{-1};B(-);\delta_T$. Substituting the two identities of Step 2 and cancelling inverses now yields
$$\delta_S^{-1};B(u_L);\delta_T=\lambda_H;\alpha^H;\rho_H^{-1}=u_H.$$
Transport of $v_L=u_L^{-1}$ is $v_H$, since functors preserve the two inverse identities. This establishes the needed compatibility for the actual representatives, including all stage associators.

proof.text: Define $e^{\mathrm{hom}}=[L_0,u_{L_0}]$ and $e^{\mathrm{inv}}=[L_0,v_{L_0}]$. Composition in the pair category is composition of representatives over a common stage. Thus the two products are $[L_0,1_{S_{L_0}}]$ and $[L_0,1_{T_{L_0}}]$, which are the identities of $S,T$ (equivalently transport the defining identity representatives to $L_0$). This gives an isomorphism $e:S\cong T$. Given any other allowed $L$, form the finite compositum $H=LL_0$. Step 3 sends both $u_L$ and $u_{L_0}$ to the identical map $u_H$. Equality after a further common-stage transport is the defining equivalence relation on representatives, so $e^{\mathrm{hom}}=[L,u_L]$. This is the required equation for every $L$, not merely an equation at the chosen initial field.
